text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Offices of Medserv, a Maltese oilfield services company, ransacked in Albania. U.S. marines evacuated director Adrian Said who said looters took away everything they could carry, including doors and windows.
- Malta-Sicily in agreement to promote two-point holidays.
- Prime Minister Alfred Sant appoints inquiry into Busietta Gardens, an apartment block built controversially in a scenic valley.

- General Workers' Union says it is not convinced new tax system will not increase prices and warns it would demand wage increases if that happens. The system, a combination of customs, a tax on products and a tax on services, is being prepared by the government to replace VAT.

- Changes expected in the role of the Employment and Training Corporation, responsible for the registration of the unemployed and training of workers. Role could be extended to other areas now handled by Labour Department.
- Elderly couple robbed of $40,000 from their home.
